basis: Defining ureteral triplication affects the urinary tract; amastia is outside axes. Frequencies of skeletal, cardiac and neurologic abnormalities are unknown.
Inherited phenylalanine metabolism disorders; substantial neurologic damage is not established across the entire umbrella, including mild forms.
Selective tooth agenesis with oligodontia in 4/4 patients; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital structural defects of the cardiac septum define the disease.
Inherited disruption of proline metabolism; neurologic and connective tissue manifestations vary across subtypes.
Mixed epithelial and stromal neoplasm arising in the kidney.
Developmental delay and intellectual impairment characterize chromosome 21q deletions; other congenital abnormalities vary with deletion extent.
Developmental delay in 15/15; scoliosis and ptosis each in 5/15 (~33%) support skeletal and eyelid involvement. Hypertrichosis alone does not establish skin damage.
Poorly specified legacy protocadherin entry without a disease definition or clinical phenotypes; neurologic assignment is provisional and cannot be confirmed from supplied data.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the condition.
DNMT3B-related immunodeficiency defines ICF1. Lasting pulmonary, intestinal and neurologic damage lacks sufficient frequency evidence; recurrent infections are separate diseases.
Maternal alloantibodies cause fetal red-cell destruction and severe anemia; hydrops-related edema and effusions alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Myotonia of skeletal and laryngeal muscles produces the defining severe neonatal episodes of airway closure.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the CNS; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis. Ocular involvement generally occurs in fewer than 30%.
Mandibular and limb defects, cleft palate and tooth agenesis define disease; airway obstruction affects 30-79%. Speech delay alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Benign neoplasm originating in bone or articular cartilage.
Inherited retinal degeneration presenting in late adulthood.
Axonal neurodegeneration and optic atrophy define disease; muscle atrophy and foot contractures affect 30-79%. Gastroesophageal reflux is a separate disease.
Developmental delay in 5/5; ventricular septal defect and patent ductus each in 2/5 (40%); finger contractures in 2/5 support joint involvement.
Collagen VI defects directly affect skeletal muscle and joints; respiratory weakness varies by severity and does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Inherited bile-transport/metabolic disorder causing recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis. Hearing loss and pancreatitis occur in only 5-29%; pruritus is a symptom.
Skin/subcutis changes and craniosynostosis define disease; lacrimal hypoplasia 5/5, visual dysfunction and conductive hearing loss 80-99%. Dental agenesis 80-99% omitted under cap.
Dysplastic adenomatous neoplasm arising in the colonic epithelium.
ABCC9-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; myocardial dysfunction, heart failure and ventricular tachycardia reported in 3/3.
Congenital interruption of the inferior vena cava is a structural venous abnormality.
